solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ghosts in Hell beyond blessedness ultimately?

indicators.note: beyond places the underworld after the letter taken from blessedness
ultimately points to the final letter of the word blessedness

parts.note: Hades is the underworld of Greek myth, a stand-in for hell

explanation.surface: A theological question: are the ghosts in hell somewhere past blessedness in the end?
explanation.definitionFit: Shades are the spirits of the dead in classical poetry, so a plural for ghosts.

clue.text: The fellow's getting loud and the row more vigorous

parts.note: the fellow is a man, he
F stands for forte, the musical direction for loud
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A man is getting noisy while the argument grows fiercer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel (rhymes with cow) but is used as a line of seats (rhymes with go).
explanation.definitionFit: Heftier means stronger or more forceful, a comparative of vigorous.

clue.text: Wife's responsibility never ending with children

indicators.note: never ending means the synonym for responsibility loses its last letter

parts.note: a duty is a responsibility

explanation.surface: A wife's duties seem endless where children are concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never ending' cuts the last letter from DUTY. 'My old dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife, from 'duchess'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch is a Cockney slang term for a man's spouse, short for duchess.

clue.text: Put off horrible vehicles, I start to cycle out

indicators.note: horrible suggests a mangled mess, so the remaining letters are jumbled
out says these letters are removed from the word vehicles
start to points to the opening letter of the word cycle

explanation.surface: Someone vows to postpone buying ugly cars and to start cycling instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes I and C (the start of 'cycle') from VEHICLES, leaving VEHLES, which 'horrible' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to postpone it, setting it aside for later.

clue.text: Accident with brewing mixture going into drink

indicators.note: going into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to sup is to drink
mash is the mixture of grain and hot water used in brewing

explanation.surface: A mishap at a brewery as the mash spills into someone's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash-up is a violent crash, especially between vehicles.

clue.text: German writer is calmer, having spent time going round church

indicators.note: going round says the shortened word wraps around another piece
having spent means the letter for time has been used up and removed

parts.note: stiller means more calm

explanation.surface: A German author grows serene after spending time around a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is calmer' tempts as one phrase, but 'is' is only a link; 'having spent' drops the time letter before the church goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and dramatist, author of the Ode to Joy.

clue.text: Heaps of food supplied during a social event

indicators.note: supplied during says one item is placed in the middle of another

parts.note: a dance is a social event
a bun is an item of food

explanation.surface: Plenty of food is laid on at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance means a plentiful supply, which is what heaps of something amounts to.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman and I, happy when set up in small house

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the abbreviation for house

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: glad means happy

explanation.surface: A Spaniard says he and I are content once settled in a cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'when set up' means read upwards, so the word for happy is reversed before joining I inside the house abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of the lower Spanish nobility, a gentleman by birth.

clue.text: Style of singing with which top tenor somehow enthrals a maiden

indicators.note: enthrals means holds captive, so one piece is held inside the other
somehow says the letters of top tenor are rearranged in some way

parts.note: M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A leading tenor captivates a young woman with his vocal technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges TOPTENOR into PORTENTO, which 'enthrals' A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Portamento is a smooth glide in pitch from one note to another, a vocal technique.

clue.text: Like a style of garment he should forfeit — out of style one not needed

indicators.note: out of style suggests things no longer in their proper form, so the letters are jumbled
not needed says the letter standing for one is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man ought to give up an unfashionable outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not needed' takes I (one) out of HESHOULDFORFEIT, and 'out of style' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-the-shoulder dress or top has a neckline that leaves the shoulders bare.

clue.text: Make untidy female in club start to listen

indicators.note: in places the pronoun inside the word for a club

parts.note: a dive is a seedy nightclub or bar
she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word listen

explanation.surface: A woman in a nightclub begins to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel hair or clothes is to make them messy.

clue.text: Woman wasn't successful, female not wanted back

indicators.note: back says the shortened word is read in reverse
not wanted means the letter for female is removed

parts.note: failed means was not successful

explanation.surface: A woman who failed finds she is not wanted back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not wanted' removes F from FAILED, giving AILED, and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia is a woman's given name, as in the cookery writer Delia Smith.

clue.text: A very quiet death taking a long time with things going on

parts.note: PP is pianissimo, the musical direction for very quiet
the end of life is death
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Someone dies quietly and slowly while life carries on around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going on' means attached on, not happening.
explanation.definitionFit: Appendages are parts added or attached to something larger, things put on.

clue.text: Heavenly place is not be be given a row of shops

indicators.note: not says the word is is left out of the longer word

parts.note: paradise is heaven

explanation.surface: Heaven is denied to a row of shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed reads 'not be be', presumably 'not to be'. In Britain a parade is a row of shops along a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade in British usage is a short street of shops, a shopping row.

clue.text: Drama in Home Counties will get performed outside, it's revealed

indicators.note: outside says the word for performed wraps around the rest

parts.note: did means performed

indicators.note: in places the drama inside the region's abbreviation

parts.note: the Home Counties lie around London in the South East, SE
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A play staged in the counties around London is put on outdoors and finally shown.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the South East, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Displayed means shown openly or put on view, so made visible.

clue.text: Pale bone possibly visible in tall skinny person

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A pale bone shows through the frame of a lanky person.
explanation.definitionFit: Beanpole is an informal word for a very tall thin person, likened to a garden pole.

clue.text: Stop taking break — weather not so good?

parts.note: a rest is a break
rain is weather that is not so good

explanation.surface: Someone takes a break because the forecast looks poor.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain someone is to stop or hold them back.

clue.text: Engineers about to embrace leader who makes an outstanding contribution to art?

definitions.text: who makes an outstanding contribution to art?

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold around, so one piece goes inside the other
about says the abbreviation is turned around

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
a boss is a leader

explanation.surface: Engineers are about to welcome a chief who gives art an outstanding contribution.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps; 'about' turns it to EMER, which embraces BOSS. 'outstanding' means raised, standing out.
explanation.definitionFit: An embosser makes raised designs, so the work literally stands out from the surface.

clue.text: Travelling via Arab state

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A journey that passes through an Arab country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab state' tempts as a single definition; the state is German and 'Arab' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bavaria is one of the federal states of Germany, with Munich its capital.

clue.text: Newspaperman picks up report of journalist finally

parts.note: to hear of something is to pick up a report of it

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word journalist

explanation.surface: A press baron catches word of a reporter at last.
explanation.definitionFit: William Randolph Hearst was a US newspaper magnate who built a vast publishing empire.

clue.text: Met on train accidentally

indicators.note: accidentally suggests the letters fell into place by chance

explanation.surface: Two people met by chance aboard a train.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to meet them unexpectedly.

clue.text: Learned person Spooner's made bed

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don, swapped the first sounds of words

parts.note: done means made, as in work done
pit is slang for bed

explanation.surface: A scholar has made the bed, as the Reverend Spooner might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: DONE PIT, said with first sounds swapped, gives 'pun dit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pundit was originally a Hindu scholar, and now an expert who gives opinions.

clue.text: Originator of dreadful wickedness?

indicators.note: the originator of a word is its first letter, here of dreadful

parts.note: evil is wickedness

explanation.surface: Who first brought terrible wickedness into the world?
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is traditionally held to be the source and author of all sin.

clue.text: It's about arousing feelings of sympathy

definitions.meaning: moving or poignant, stirring tender emotion

explanation.surface: Someone explains that the story is all about stirring compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Touching means both concerning a topic and emotionally moving.

clue.text: Nasty woman's way of speaking in dance

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for a dance

parts.note: the hay is an old country dance
RP is Received Pronunciation, the standard British accent

explanation.surface: A spiteful woman's manner of talking is heard at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: RP, Received Pronunciation, is the prestige accent of southern England; the hay (or hey) is a country dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpy is a grasping, shrewish woman, after the winged monsters of Greek myth.

clue.text: Ring my gardener about shifting boundaries in plot?

indicators.note: about suggests moving round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Phone the gardener about moving the fences around the vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a garden bed, matching the gardener, but means a political scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerrymandering is redrawing electoral districts to favour one party, a scheme of moved borders.

clue.text: Substitute starts to seem trustworthy and will get elected

indicators.note: starts to points to the opening letters of the words seem and trustworthy

parts.note: taken as written
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A replacement candidate begins to look reliable and wins the vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a replacement who takes another's place for a time.

clue.text: Actress as someone to get you in stitches in the auditorium?

indicators.note: in the auditorium means as heard by an audience, so by sound

parts.words: someone to get you in stitches
parts.note: a tailor sews, putting you into a stitched suit

explanation.surface: An actress described as a comic who has the audience in fits of laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in stitches' suggests laughter, but here a clothes-maker sews you into a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Taylor was a celebrated Hollywood film star.
